mechanism_narrative: A low federal funds rate indicates an accommodative monetary policy, which may stimulate economic growth and lead to positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in 60% of periods following low FEDFUNDS.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate below 4% signals a strong labor market, which may boost consumer spending and lead to positive S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 does not show positive returns when UNRATE is below 4%.

mechanism_narrative: Rising federal funds rates alongside falling unemployment indicates tightening monetary policy, which may lead to negative S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: If positive returns occur despite the trigger conditions.

mechanism_narrative: GDP growth indicates strong demand, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: If GDP growth does not correlate with positive S&P returns.

mechanism_narrative: Increasing payroll employment suggests economic strength, leading to positive S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: If payroll growth does not lead to positive returns.

mechanism_narrative: High industrial production suggests strong supply, leading to positive S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: If industrial production does not correlate with positive returns.

mechanism_narrative: Rising retail sales and employment indicate strong demand, leading to positive S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: If returns are negative despite the trigger conditions.

mechanism_narrative: Rising federal funds rates in a tightening cycle may lead to negative S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: If positive returns occur despite rising FEDFUNDS.
